title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is an image-alteration failure inside a promotional workflow, not a model error in the ordinary sense. A photograph of real, named students was edited so that one student's likeness was replaced and others were reshaped, and the result was published as institutional advertising. The system produced a person who was not in the original photograph and presented her as though she were part of the scene.

The failure sits at the point where generated or edited imagery enters published material. Stanford's own policy barred using AI to produce or alter images of its people, events, facilities, research or achievements, and the university said both the alteration and the failure to disclose it broke that rule. Catching it required a review step before the banners went up, one that compared the published image against the source photograph and checked it against the policy, and a disclosure requirement that would have surfaced the edit even if the review did not.

What the reporting does not establish is intent. No account given here says who made the edit, why it was made, or whether anyone was disciplined, and a policy violation confirmed by the university is not by itself a finding about motive.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology at Stanford, appeared in a 2024 Lunar New Year photo with two other students. The university's dining service posted it online the next day. When Stanford used the image on banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated, though he also saw a comedic element.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to change the original image. The university said its policy strictly bans using A.I. to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said both the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
